package_info.package_name: polyfill.io (CDN service, as used by npm packages such as create-polyfill-service-url, dynamic-polyfill, etc.)
package_info.package_manager: npm (and any web project embedding the CDN)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using cdn.polyfill.io after domain transfer to Funnull (Feb 2024 onward)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious JavaScript after a change in domain ownership in February 2024. The CDN injected code that redirected mobile users to scam or phishing sites, impacting any website or npm package embedding scripts from cdn.polyfill.io. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the malicious code was automatically delivered to all dependent sites and packages, enabling large-scale user redirection and potential credential theft or malware delivery.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the script is loaded and executed by the browser)
required_permissions: redirect capability (to navigate users to external domains)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Detects if the visitor is using a mobile device by inspecting the user agent string. If a mobile device is detected, the code forcibly redirects the user to an attacker-controlled scam or phishing website.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code performs user-agent sniffing to identify mobile devices and then immediately redirects users to an external, attacker-controlled domain. Such behavior is not expected in a polyfill library, which should only provide compatibility shims and not alter user navigation or interact with the DOM in this manner.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate polyfill library is expected to provide JavaScript compatibility features for older browsers without modifying page navigation, performing user-agent checks for redirection, or interacting with the DOM beyond polyfill logic. Redirecting users to external domains is a clear violation of these expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User-agent detection and redirection can be legitimate in first-party web applications for mobile optimization or A/B testing, but it is never appropriate in a third-party polyfill or utility library, especially one loaded from a CDN and intended solely for browser compatibility.
key_indicators: Presence of user-agent sniffing logic targeting mobile devices within a polyfill script
Immediate assignment to window.location.href, causing forced navigation
Redirection to domains unrelated to the polyfill.io service or the website's legitimate business
Injected code appended to or obfuscated within a widely used third-party library
Behavior only present after a specific domain ownership change (post-Feb 2024)

attack_chain.action: A website or npm package includes a script tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io (e.g., <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script>), or programmatically loads the polyfill.io CDN in its source code.
attack_chain.leads_to: The browser requests and loads the JavaScript file from the CDN.

attack_chain.action: The compromised CDN endpoint delivers malicious JavaScript code to the user's browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious code is executed in the context of the website visitor's browser.

attack_chain.action: The malicious code checks if the visitor is on a mobile device by inspecting the user agent. If a mobile device is detected, the code redirects the user to a scam or phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: The user is sent to an attacker-controlled landing page, enabling further attacks such as credential theft, malware delivery, or scam operations.

behavioral_signatures: Third-party JavaScript libraries (especially polyfills) performing user-agent sniffing and conditional redirection
Unexpected window.location.href assignments within polyfill or utility libraries
Polyfill scripts containing code unrelated to browser compatibility, such as DOM manipulation for navigation
Presence of obfuscated or appended redirect logic in scripts loaded from cdn.polyfill.io
file_indicators: References to cdn.polyfill.io in script tags, HTML templates, or npm package source code
Polyfill JavaScript files (e.g., polyfill.min.js) containing suspicious or appended redirect logic
Scripts from cdn.polyfill.io with code segments matching user-agent sniffing and redirection patterns
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) requests to cdn.polyfill.io after February 2024
Redirections from pages loading polyfill.io scripts to known scam, phishing, or unrelated external domains
Network traffic showing initial load from cdn.polyfill.io followed by immediate navigation to attacker-controlled URLs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan web applications and npm packages for script tags or dependencies referencing cdn.polyfill.io. Analyze loaded JavaScript for unexpected behaviors such as user-agent sniffing and window.location redirects, especially in polyfill or utility libraries. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to block or report scripts from untrusted or recently transferred domains. Employ Subresource Integrity (SRI) to ensure third-party scripts have not been tampered with. Flag any polyfill or utility library that performs DOM redirection or network requests to suspicious or unrelated domains. Monitor for outbound requests to cdn.polyfill.io and subsequent redirections to known scam or phishing domains.
